Build the Documents and templates module (templates, document assembly and generation, bulk download and extra versioning tools) exactly as docs/modules/documents/SPEC.md specifies, in modules/documents/. The spec is the assignment: it records how Nolan PMS Unified does this today and every decision; reuse that working approach, written clean. Read togavsu-core-prd.md section 9 (module interface and 9.9 data rules) and use examples/matter-clock as the working reference for manifest, signing, migrations, frames, events and tests. The module is self-contained: its own container, its own schema mod_<id>, core records reached only through the core API with its approved scopes, core records linked by id with ON DELETE RESTRICT, no table that duplicates a core record, files stored as core file records, signed with the marketplace signing path matter-clock uses. Every external service sits behind an adapter interface; tests use the fake adapter and synthetic data only, never real credentials, real mailboxes, real payment or signing services, or real client data. Keys are admin-entered settings at runtime. Put the module's Go tests in your owned paths so the Core tests job runs them against real Postgres, installing the signed package through the module runtime as the matter-clock acceptance tests do; cover every MOD acceptance criterion in the spec, failure cases included. If the module needs a core endpoint, scope, event or hook the core lacks, do not edit core code: implement against the contract the spec names, keep that test skipped only where the core piece is missing, and list each core change under 'Core changes for integrate-modules' in the PR body. The module-core lane builds the spec's core changes in parallel and integrate-modules turns those tests on. Never edit outside your owned paths, .github/, the PRD, the spec, controller files or review gates. If the same problem survives three fix passes, stop and report it plainly instead of trying again.
